svg.title: PrismGate detailed architecture
svg.desc: Client apps flow through gateway ingress, a routing and decision engine with six numbered steps, into three backend tiers (small tier split into CPU, GPU, specialized accelerator, and burst GPU sub-clusters; mid tier as a self-hosted GPU cluster; frontier tier as an external API), converging into LangSmith tracing and a FinOps dashboard.
svg.text: Client apps through routing, self-hosted compute, and observability
Authenticates the caller, resolves its app identity and quota, and attaches request context
(app id, declared SLA, data-sensitivity flag) before anything else runs.
2 · ROUTING & DECISION ENGINE — HOW THE MODEL CHOICE GETS MADE
Pulls signals off the request: prompt token count, task-type hint from the calling app, whether tools/agent-loop steps
are declared, and a data-sensitivity flag (PII, contractual, regulated data).
Blends a rule-based score (token count, keyword/task-type signal) with an optional learned classifier's score. Output
is a single complexity value from 0 to 1. Roadmap: replace the rule-based half with a model trained on real routing
Compliance rules run regardless of the complexity score. A data-sensitivity flag forces the small, self-hosted tier no
matter how complex the task looks — the request never reaches an external API.
Independently of where the request is actually routed, prices what it would have cost on the frontier tier with no
cache. This funds the savings % reported on the FinOps dashboard.
Exact-match today (hash of the normalized prompt); semantic match (embedding similarity) is next on the roadmap. A hit
returns the cached response immediately, at zero cost, skipping every step below.
Checks the requesting app's spend-so-far against its daily budget. Over budget blocks the request before it reaches a
model — zero cost, zero exposure — rather than after.
data_sensitivity flag present → forced to small tier, regardless of score
3 · BACKEND TIERS — WHERE EACH REQUEST ACTUALLY RUNS
Quantized 3B–7B models on CPU inference (e.g. GGUF
via llama.cpp). No GPU cost — the default for high-
volume, low-complexity traffic like FAQ and wiki
Same complexity band, but for apps with a tighter
latency SLA than CPU inference can meet.
Small/quantized models on shared GPU capacity.
Optional: Inferentia/TPU-class chips for one narrow,
very high-volume workload (e.g. embeddings at scale)
where custom silicon beats general GPU cost-per-
Elastic, preemptible capacity for traffic spikes and
batchable, non-latency-critical work. Priced at spot
rates; the router only sends here what can tolerate
Mid-size open model (13B–70B class) on dedicated
Reasoning: this band carries the bulk of request
volume, so owning the GPUs amortizes fast — the
per-token cost falls below the API-equivalent
tier once utilization is steady, while quality
stays close enough for non-frontier work.
OpenAI or Anthropic's top-tier model, selected
Reasoning: reserved for the ~10–15% of traffic
that actually needs frontier capability. No
infrastructure to run, always the current model
generation, billed per token — the right
tradeoff at low volume for this tier
4 · EVERY PATH CONVERGES BACK THROUGH OBSERVABILITY
Every step above (classify, policy check, cache, budget, model call)
is logged as its own span, tagged by app — filterable and
Aggregates spans into cost per app, cost per outcome, cache hit
rate, and savings vs. the no-gateway baseline — the numbers
5 · WHY SELF-HOSTED COMPUTE FOR THE SMALL AND MID TIERS
Rather than routing everything to external APIs
by policy for some data classes,
